description: Cross-language failure contract for Monark's Google Drive cloud-storage auth/refresh/OAuth paths (issue #28, D4). Rust derives every `message` by rendering the real AuthFailureClass templates (see `src-tauri/src/commands/errors.rs`) and the frontend classifies those exact strings with `classifyCloudFailure` (`src/services/cloudStorageErrors.ts`). Test-only: no production module imports this file; `src/test/helpers/authFailureContract.ts` is the single TS loader. The Rust `include_str!` consumer (`src-tauri/src/commands/errors.rs`) lands with T12 and the TS consumer tests with T13 — until then no consumer re-derives the `message` bytes (the schema itself is enforced at load by the TS loader).

templates.TransientLocalStorage: network or local storage error while {context}: {cause}

contexts.refresh: refreshing the Google Drive access token
contexts.codeExchange: exchanging the Google Drive authorization code
contexts.tokenParse: parsing the Google Drive token response
contexts.loadConfig: loading the Google Drive provider configuration
contexts.tokenPersistence: saving the Google Drive tokens that Google already issued

cases.description: A request-level failure (DNS/connect/timeout) during the access-token refresh: `StorageError::Network` reaches `classify_refresh_failure`'s Transient arm, rendered with the plain `Transient` template. Note the cause carries the `StorageError::Network` Display prefix (`Network error: …`) because the arm interpolates `error.to_string()`.
cases.cause: Network error: Network error during token refresh: error sending request
cases.message: network error while refreshing the Google Drive access token: Network error: Network error during token refresh: error sending request

cases.description: A non-2xx token-endpoint response carried structurally as `StorageError::HttpStatus` (issue #28, D3). A transient status (408/429/5xx) drops the upstream `body` — that (dropped) body is adversarial in the producer tests (`connection reset, authentication required`), while the pinned cause here is the status prefix only: the point is that no body ever reaches the rendered message, keeping the class purely `Transient`/`NETWORK_ERROR`.
cases.cause: Failed to refresh access token (503 Service Unavailable)
cases.message: network error while refreshing the Google Drive access token: Failed to refresh access token (503 Service Unavailable)

cases.description: Persisting the freshly rotated tokens failed on the OS keychain (`StorageError::Keychain`). This is the fourth, distinct template rendered by `AuthFailureClass::into_command_error_local_storage` (review finding m4): it names the *local* cause while keeping the `network` keyword the frontend routes on, so it stays `NETWORK_ERROR`/`transient` — the refresh token is unchanged, so the next attempt is legitimate. The real producer appends the OS keyring error to the cause (`keychain.rs`); the fixture pins the stable prefix only, with the dynamic tail elided.
cases.cause: Keychain error: Failed to set keychain secret
cases.message: network or local storage error while refreshing the Google Drive access token: Keychain error: Failed to set keychain secret

cases.description: Google refused the refresh token (HTTP 400 + `invalid_grant`, or an explicitly revoked token): `StorageError::Authentication` reaches `classify_refresh_failure`'s `AuthRejection` arm. The provider's fixed wording (`Google Drive refresh token is invalid or has been revoked. Please re-authenticate.`) already contains the `authentication`/`re-authenticate` keywords the frontend keys on, so no redaction applies (the AuthRejection class only redacts the retryable keywords `network`/`connection`).
cases.cause: Google Drive refresh token is invalid or has been revoked. Please re-authenticate.
cases.message: authentication failed while refreshing the Google Drive access token (re-authenticate): Google Drive refresh token is invalid or has been revoked. Please re-authenticate.

cases.description: The OAuth authorization-code exchange got HTTP 400 + `invalid_grant` from the token endpoint: `classify_token_endpoint_status` classifies it `AuthRejection` and `exchange_google_drive_code` renders the cause as `the token endpoint returned HTTP status {status}: {bounded_body}` (the upstream body is kept, since it is genuinely useful and the AuthRejection bucket has the highest frontend precedence).
cases.cause: the token endpoint returned HTTP status 400 Bad Request: {"error":"invalid_grant"}
cases.message: authentication failed while exchanging the Google Drive authorization code (re-authenticate): the token endpoint returned HTTP status 400 Bad Request: {"error":"invalid_grant"}

cases.description: The tokens were obtained but could not be persisted (config write / OS keychain). The authorization code is single-use (already spent), so the failure is terminal for the OAuth state (`keep_state == false`) even though the underlying cause looks like retryable IO — the lifecycle cannot be derived from the class alone (review finding MAJOR-2). The message is keyword-free by construction (`OPERATION_FAILED`, a terminal bucket) and honest about the remediation (the user must sign in again).
cases.cause: the tokens were obtained but could not be persisted; please sign in again (Keychain error: the secret service is not available)
cases.message: unexpected failure while saving the Google Drive tokens that Google already issued: the tokens were obtained but could not be persisted; please sign in again (Keychain error: the secret service is not available)

cases.description: The OAuth `state` is unknown or has expired: `oauth_state_terminal_error()` classifies it `Other` (the request never reached Google, so it is neither a credential rejection nor retryable). The cause contains the routing keyword `expired`, which the `Other` class redacts in full (`Other` redacts every routing keyword), pinning the real production string `… has [redacted]` — a keyword-free message that lands in the frontend's conservative terminal `OPERATION_FAILED` bucket.
cases.cause: the OAuth state is unknown or has expired
cases.message: unexpected failure while validating the OAuth state: the OAuth state is unknown or has [redacted]

cases.description: The OAuth callback could not resolve the Google Drive provider config (precondition failure, not a credential rejection): reported as `Other` (terminal) with a keyword-free message that lands in the frontend's conservative `OPERATION_FAILED` bucket.
cases.cause: the provider has no stored configuration
cases.message: unexpected failure while loading the Google Drive provider configuration: the provider has no stored configuration
